arxiv-2111-10527.title: Pre-scaling and Codebook Design for Joint Radar and Communication Based on Index Modulation
arxiv-2111-10527.creator: Shengyang Chen, Aryan Kaushik, and Christos Masouros
arxiv-2111-10527.description: Abstract This paper develops an efficient index modulation (IM) approach for the joint radar-communication (JRC) system based on a multi-carrier multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. The communication information is embedded into the transmitted radar pulses by selecting the corresponding indices of the carrier frequencies and antenna allocations, providing two degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2204-11543.title: Massive particle acceleration on a photonic chip via spatial-temporal modulation
arxiv-2204-11543.creator: Mai Zhang, Xie-hang Yu, Xin-Biao Xu, Guang-Can Guo, Chang-Ling Zou
arxiv-2204-11543.description: Abstract Recently, the spectral manipulation of single photons has been achieved through spatial-temporal modulation of the optical refractive index. Here, we generalize this mechanism to massive particles, i.e. realizing the acceleration or deceleration of particles through the spatial-temporal modulation of potential induced by lasers.

arxiv-2205-14400.title: Agent-based Simulation of District-based Elections
arxiv-2205-14400.creator: Adway Mitra
arxiv-2205-14400.description: Abstract In district-based elections, electors cast votes in their respective districts. In each district, the party with maximum votes wins the corresponding “seat” in the governing body. The election result is based on the number of seats won by different parties.

arxiv-2306-00528.title: Neuronal Cell Type Classification using Deep Learning
arxiv-2306-00528.creator: Ofek Ophir, Orit Shefi, Ofir Lindenbaum
arxiv-2306-00528.description: Abstract The brain is likely the most complex organ, given the variety of functions it controls, the number of cells it comprises, and their corresponding diversity. Studying and identifying neurons, the brain’s primary building blocks, is a crucial milestone and essential for understanding brain function in health and disease.

arxiv-2309-12986.title: A precise determination of the strong-coupling constant from the recoil of Z Z bosons with the ATLAS experiment at s = 8 \sqrt{s}=8 TeV
arxiv-2309-12986.description: Abstract The coupling constant of the strong force is determined from the transverse-momentum distribution of Z Z bosons produced in 8 TeV proton–proton collisions at the LHC and recorded by the ATLAS experiment. The Z Z -boson cross sections are measured in the full phase space of the decay leptons using 15.

arxiv-2310-08271.creator: Leilei Yu, Yunghsiang S. Han, Jiasheng Yuan, Zhongpei Zhang
arxiv-2310-08271.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Leilei Yu, Yunghsiang S. Han, Jiasheng Yuan, Zhongpei Zhang. Binary array codes are widely used in storage systems to prevent data loss, such as the Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID). arxiv-2404-10447.title: Millisecond-resolved infrared spectroscopy study of polymer brush swelling dynamics
arxiv-2404-10447.creator: K.F.A. Jorissen, L.B. Veldscholte, M. Odijk, S. de Beer
arxiv-2404-10447.description: Abstract We present the study of millisecond-resolved polymer brush swelling dynamics using infrared spectroscopy with a custom-built quantum cascade laser-based infrared spectrometer at a 1 kHz 1\text{\,}\mathrm{kHz} sampling rate after averaging. By cycling the humidity of the environment of the polymer brush, we are able to measure the swelling dynamics sequentially at different wavenumbers.

arxiv-2407-07299.title: Random Reed–Solomon Codes Achieve the Half-Singleton Bound for Insertions and Deletions over Linear-Sized Alphabets
arxiv-2407-07299.creator: Roni Con, Zeyu Guo, Ray Li, Zihan Zhang
arxiv-2407-07299.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Roni Con, Zeyu Guo, Ray Li, Zihan Zhang. In this paper, we prove that with high probability, random Reed–Solomon codes approach the half-Singleton bound — the optimal rate versus error tradeoff for linear insdel codes — with linear-sized alphabets.

arxiv-2504-19236.title: Neutron source-based event reconstruction algorithm in large liquid scintillator detectors
arxiv-2504-19236.creator: Akira Takenaka e1,addr1, Zhangming Chen addr2, Arran Freegard addr2, Junting Huang addr2, Jiaqi Hui addr1, Haojing Lai addr2, Rui Li addr2, Yilin Liao addr2, Jianglai Liu addr1, addr2, Yue Meng addr2, Iwan Morton-Blake addr1, Ziqian Xiang addr2, Ping Zhang addr2
arxiv-2504-19236.description: Abstract We developed an event reconstruction algorithm, applicable to large liquid scintillator detectors, built primarily upon neutron calibration data. We employ a likelihood method using photon detection time and charge information from individual photomultiplier tubes. Detector response tables in the likelihood function were derived from americium-carbon neutron source events, 2.

arxiv-2508-10958.title: Probing phase transitions and microscopic interactions in quasi-topological black holes
arxiv-2508-10958.creator: Apurba Tiwari, Randeep Kaur, Aruri Devaraju, Jaya Prakash Kode, Apparao Damarasingu, Silamanthula Hari Krishna, Akshay Gharat
arxiv-2508-10958.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Apurba Tiwari, Randeep Kaur, Aruri Devaraju, Jaya Prakash Kode, Apparao Damarasingu, Silamanthula Hari Krishna, Akshay Gharat. In this paper, we examine the thermodynamic geometry of four-dimensional quasi-topological black holes by computing the Ruppeiner scalar curvature ℛ \mathcal{R} which serves as an empirical tool to describe the nature of interactions among black hole microstructures. In four dimensions, we write novel black hole solutions within the framework of generalized quasi-topological gravity, extended through a fundamental p p -form field.

arxiv-2509-22521.title: Resource-efficient universal photonic processor based on time-multiplexed hybrid architectures
arxiv-2509-22521.creator: Jonas Lammers, Laura Ares, Federico Pegoraro, Philip Held, Benjamin Brecht, Jan Sperling, Christine Silberhorn
arxiv-2509-22521.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jonas Lammers, Laura Ares, Federico Pegoraro, Philip Held, Benjamin Brecht, Jan Sperling, Christine Silberhorn. For the ever-growing field of quantum information processing, large-scale, efficient multi-port interferometers serving as photonic processors are required. In this context, the suitability of quantum walks as the interferometric base for universal computation has been theoretically proven. In this work, we bridge the gap between theoretical proposals and state-of-the-art experimental capabilities by providing the recipe for the implementation of a universal photonic processor in discrete-time quantum walks.

arxiv-2510-02433.title: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals in relativistic accretion discs
arxiv-2510-02433.creator: Francisco Duque, Laura Sberna, Andrew Spiers, Rodrigo Vicente
arxiv-2510-02433.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francisco Duque, Laura Sberna, Andrew Spiers, Rodrigo Vicente. We compute relativistic Lindblad torques for circular, equatorial extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) embedded in relativistic thin accretion discs, including spinning black hole configurations. We find that relativistic effects can amplify the magnitude of these torques by orders of magnitude in the strong-field regime, and that the torque can even reverse direction as the EMRI approaches the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO).

arxiv-2601-15317.title: The Impossibility of Cohesion Without Fragmentation
arxiv-2601-15317.creator: Daisuke Hirota
arxiv-2601-15317.description: Abstract Why do division and cohesion so often intensify together? This paper provides a structural answer by developing a static theory of relation maintenance based on minimal positional constraints. We model social relations as subject to minimum conditions defined over an abstract position space.

pmc-10575265.title: CANAttack: Assessing Vulnerabilities within Controller Area Network
pmc-10575265.creator: Damilola Oladimeji, Amar Rasheed, Cihan Varol, Mohamed Baza, Hani Alshahrani, Abdullah Baz, Alessandra Rizzardi
pmc-10575265.description: Current vehicles include electronic features that provide ease and convenience to drivers. These electronic features or nodes rely on in-vehicle communication protocols to ensure functionality. One of the most-widely adopted in-vehicle protocols on the market today is the Controller Area Network, popularly referred to as the CAN bus. The CAN bus is utilized in various modern, sophisticated vehicles.

pmc-11510355.title: Dehydration and Suboptimal Sleep Aggravate Early Renal Impairment in Children: Longitudinal Findings from the PROC Study
pmc-11510355.creator: Menglong Li, Huidi Xiao, Nubiya Amaerjiang, Bipin Thapa, Wen Shu, Yeerlin Asihaer, Mengying Guan, Sten H Vermund, Zhiyong Zou, Dayong Huang, Yifei Hu, Hiroshi Itoh, Masashi Mizuno, Maria Luz Fernandez
pmc-11510355.description: Background: While dehydration is associated with pediatric renal impairment, the regulation of hydration status can be affected by sleep. However, the interaction of hydration and sleep on kidney health remains unclear. Methods: We conducted a cohort study among 1914 healthy primary school children from October 2018 to November 2019 in Beijing, China.

pmc-11672817.title: Genetic Analysis of Days Open in Moroccan Holstein Using Different Models to Account for Censored Data
pmc-11672817.creator: Narjice Chafai, Bouabid Badaoui, Michael E Davis
pmc-11672817.description: Simple SummaryReproductive performance is a critical factor for the economic success and long-term viability of dairy herds. Intense selection for milk production has resulted in a decline in fertility traits in Holstein cows, leading to negative consequences for the industry. To combat this, incorporating fertility traits into the genetic evaluation is a potential solution.

pmc-12539362.title: Monosodium Iodoacetate Induces Knee Osteoarthritis in Rats in a Dose- and Time-Dependent Manner
pmc-12539362.creator: Min Song, Weichang Han, Jingyi Li, Gaoyi Wu, Haibo Yu, Qing Yuan, Jiani Yu
pmc-12539362.description: BackgroundKnee osteoarthritis (KOA) is indeed a major global health issue, characterized as the most common form of osteoarthritis. It affects millions of people worldwide, leading to joint pain, stiffness, and functional limitations. As life expectancy increases and populations age, KOA’s impact on quality of life and public health systems becomes more pronounced.

pmc-12590262.title: Correlation between gingival fibroblast cell viability and degree of conversion of resin composites at different light-curing tip distances
pmc-12590262.creator: Atieh Hashemian, Mahshid Hodjat, Marjan Behroozibakhsh
pmc-12590262.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of light-curing tip distance on the degree of conversion (DC), as well as on the cell viability. The study also aimed to assess the correlation between DC% and cell viability at different light-curing tip distances.

pmc-12644503.title: GlycoGenius: a streamlined high-throughput glycan composition identification tool
pmc-12644503.creator: Hector F Loponte, Jing Zheng, Yajie Ding, Isadora A Oliveira, Kristoffer Basse, Adriane R Todeschini, Peter L Horvatovich, Guinevere S M Lageveen-Kammeijer
pmc-12644503.description: Mass spectrometry is recognized as the gold standard for glycan analysis, yet the complexity of the generated data hampers progress in glycobiology, as existing tools lack full automation, requiring extensive manual effort. We introduce GlycoGenius, an open-source program offering an automated workflow for glycomics data analysis, featuring an intuitive graphical interface.

pmc-12661047.title: Interval-aware optimal control of PMSG-based wind energy conversion systems via piecewise Chebyshev inclusion
pmc-12661047.creator: Navid Razmjooy
pmc-12661047.description: Due to the ever-increasing demand for wind energy, control strategies must be developed that can efficiently extract energy while ensuring system stability. Nevertheless, with significant excursion uncertainties like parametric variation, unmodeled dynamics, and environmental variations jeopardizing control performance and system reliability, the Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) is subject to significant interval uncertainties.

pmc-12748337.title: Etiologies of intermediate uveitis in a tertiary center: an age-oriented medical assessment?
pmc-12748337.creator: P. Mansuy, T. El-Jammal, R. Jacquot, T. Mathis, L. Kodjikian, Pascal Sève
pmc-12748337.description: PurposeTo analyze the distribution of intermediate uveitis (IU) etiologies by age in order to guide the diagnostic approach.MethodsWe conducted a monocentric retrospective study of 126 adult patients referred to an internal medicine department at a tertiary center with a diagnosis of intermediate uveitis of unknown cause between July 2002 and April 2023.

pmc-13214161.description: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of numerous neurodegenerative, psychiatric, and chronic pain disorders and can be assessed in vivo with 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) positron emission tomography (PET). However, conventional quantification methods of TSPO PET are limited and often overlook the spatial relationships between regional signals.

pmc-13647640.title: Laparoscopic enterolithotomy for large gallstone ileus in an elderly high-risk patient: a case report
pmc-13647640.creator: Marei Alshandeer
pmc-13647640.description: BackgroundGallstone ileus is an uncommon complication of cholelithiasis leading to mechanical small bowel obstruction that typically affects geriatric populations with significant baseline medical conditions. The optimal management approach is highly debated, specifically when choosing between simple emergency enterolithotomy alone or a complex one-stage definitive biliary procedure in high-risk patients.
